logs.summary: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has become the fastest-growing ever, with cases surging above 1,000 and the death toll reaching 600. The outbreak has spread to new provinces including Tshopo and Haut-Uele, and the first case outside Africa has been confirmed in France. Response efforts are hampered by funding shortages, unpaid health workers, and the closure of USAID, while new diagnostic tests and treatment trials offer hope.

news.body: HONG KONG, July 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) Hong Kong yesterday held an opening ceremony for its 'Keep Life Breathing' Roving Exhibition. As a key part of its annual 'MSF Day' campaign, the exhibition will tour three locations throughout July: The Wai, Festival Walk, and TKO Plaza. It showcases real-life stories of MSF providing emergency medical humanitarian assistance to people affected by protracted conflicts and crises. The event also features an Ebola disease-themed zone, which aims to deepen public awareness and understanding of the ongoing outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC).

AP photos captured funerals for the Medina Alvarez family and other victims in La Guaira.

logs.summary:
Ukraine struck additional warehouses of Russia's top online retailer Wildberries and intensified attacks on Ozon, causing economic disruption. In leadership moves, President Zelensky replaced the commander-in-chief with Mykhailo Drapatyi and fired Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov, sparking protests. Meanwhile, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio met with Russia's Lavrov in Manila, expressing readiness to help end the war but noting no quick deal is imminent.
Ukrainian strikes on Russia's Wildberries warehouses produced massive pillars of black smoke as fires raged at the facilities. Russia, stretched by Ukraine's drone attacks on its Black Sea Fleet, has pulled all warships from the Mediterranean Sea. Both sides have increased bridge strikes to disrupt resupply networks, indicating expectations of a prolonged stalemate, while the Kremlin warned against optimism on peace following the Rubio-Lavrov meeting.
The EU passed its 21st sanctions package with 218 new designations targeting Russia, including vessels that refuel shadow fleet tankers. Ukrainian strikes continued to hit Russian Wildberries warehouses, while new airstrikes caused deaths in both Ukraine and Russia, and a drone was shot down over NATO airspace.

logs.summary:
On August 15-16, Ukraine launched a record 822-drone attack on Russia, striking Moscow's largest Wildberries warehouse and other targets, killing at least six people across Russia. Escalating strikes killed 19 people across both countries, including six in Belgorod from a Ukrainian missile attack. Meanwhile, Russian state development bank VEB fired chief economist Andrei Klepach after he warned Russia is losing the war of attrition, and Poland's defense minister stated the country is preparing for war with Russia.

logs.summary:
The U.S. and Iran have paused attacks and resumed diplomatic efforts to end the conflict, with mediators reporting progress and talks focused on reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Meanwhile, the Pentagon quietly removed four recent troop deaths from its official Iran war death toll, reclassifying them in a new category, sparking controversy. Additional concerns include the U.S.'s dangerously low weaponry supply and growing public skepticism over the war’s costs and duration.
Mediators reported that neither the U.S. nor Iran conducted any attacks for three consecutive days, signaling progress in ceasefire efforts. New polls indicate that only one in three Americans now support the war, the lowest reading since the conflict began, and a majority view it as going "very badly." The Pentagon continued to face scrutiny over its reclassification of four troop deaths from the conflict.

logs.summary:
The 60-day ceasefire framework between the U.S. and Iran expired on August 17 with no peace deal, as President Trump threatened to "bomb the s*** out of" Oman if it interferes with Strait of Hormuz negotiations. Iran shifted to a "fully offensive" posture, offered bounties of up to $60,000 for killing or capturing U.S. troops, and reportedly has a secret plan to escalate the war, while oil prices rose above $91/barrel and Middle Eastern airlines projected $4.3 billion in losses for 2026.
President Trump threatened to bomb Oman because he is unhappy with the country's deal with Iran to manage Strait of Hormuz traffic, and posted that no talks or conversations are scheduled with Iran. His approval rating sank to a presidency-low of 33% as the war drags on, with oil prices rising and government borrowing costs hitting multi-decade highs amid fading peace hopes.

incidents.summary:
New developments three weeks after the Kumamoto earthquake include a ferry anchored at Yatsushiro port offering free meals, bathing, medical services, and a children's play area to evacuees. Security footage emerged showing a massive crack appearing in a rice paddy in Yatsushiro at the moment the quake struck, while the disaster also severely impacted Kumamoto's traditional tatami industry. Authorities shifted focus to preventing deaths from prolonged displacement, and Kumamoto's mascot Kumamon visited a school sheltering both students and evacuees to spread cheer.
New reports three weeks after the Kumamoto earthquake highlight emerging challenges: impostors dressed as military personnel are looting abandoned homes, and authorities are struggling to deliver relief to evacuees not staying in designated shelters. The Japanese government plans to craft a stimulus package for tourism and aid by the end of August. A comparative analysis of Japan's and Venezuela's earthquake responses also references the disaster.

logs.summary:
A powerful earthquake, initially measured at magnitude 7.1 (later revised to 6.8), struck Kumamoto Prefecture in southern Japan on July 28, 2026, at 4:27 p.m. local time. The quake caused the partial collapse of the Aeon Mall in Kashima, trapping many people and leaving an unknown number dead, while injuring at least 50 others and causing widespread damage including fires, power outages, and damage to historic Kumamoto Castle.
A 7.1-magnitude earthquake struck southern Japan's Kyushu island near Kumamoto on July 28, 2026, causing a shopping mall to partially collapse with multiple people trapped and feared dead. The quake knocked out power to thousands of homes, ruptured roads, triggered a temporary tsunami advisory, and left dozens injured, with up to 30 mall employees missing after an explosion.

logs.summary:
New developments three weeks after the Kumamoto earthquake include a ferry anchored at Yatsushiro port offering free meals, bathing, medical services, and a children's play area to evacuees. Security footage emerged showing a massive crack appearing in a rice paddy in Yatsushiro at the moment the quake struck, while the disaster also severely impacted Kumamoto's traditional tatami industry. Authorities shifted focus to preventing deaths from prolonged displacement, and Kumamoto's mascot Kumamon visited a school sheltering both students and evacuees to spread cheer.
New reports three weeks after the Kumamoto earthquake highlight emerging challenges: impostors dressed as military personnel are looting abandoned homes, and authorities are struggling to deliver relief to evacuees not staying in designated shelters. The Japanese government plans to craft a stimulus package for tourism and aid by the end of August. A comparative analysis of Japan's and Venezuela's earthquake responses also references the disaster.

incidents.summary:
As of mid-August 2026, drought impacts continue globally: Lake Mead and Lake Powell both hit record lows, with human remains surfacing at Lake Mead's Boulder Beach. In India, satellite data shows 64% of farmland under drought stress, while Oklahoma endures an extended heat wave with temperatures reaching 106°F. In the UK, England's drought reveals a ghost village beneath Rutland Water reservoir, and hosepipe bans now affect 27 million people. Colorado reports a surge in bear sightings due to diminished wild food sources, and a record-early champagne harvest in France highlights ongoing climate impacts on agriculture.
Severe drought expands in Minnesota, threatening farms, while in Florida, drought is cited as a factor in increased alligator attacks. In Asia, Skymet cuts its 2026 monsoon forecast to 85% of the long-period average, assigning a 70% chance of drought conditions. Meanwhile, new research indicates drought extremes are intensifying more rapidly than in the past, and Colorado launches the Rye Resurgence Project to promote drought-tolerant grain.

logs.summary:
A severe drought is affecting multiple regions globally as of late July 2026. In Europe, an "exceptionally serious" drought has hit half of England and all of Wales, while the Rhine River dropped to its lowest ever level in the Netherlands and the Danube reached record lows in Budapest, disrupting tourism and industry. In the United States, drought conditions worsened in states like Minnesota and Michigan, while other areas like the Grand Strand in South Carolina are lifting drought management plans, and parts of Virginia and North Carolina are seeing improvements.
New drought developments include worsening conditions in Maine and Minnesota, with 35% of Minnesota in severe drought, while South Carolina's Lowcountry remains under extreme drought despite summer storms. In Europe, record-low river levels continue to disrupt power output and transport, and wildfire risk is elevated across the continent. Jamaica faces a potential $500 million drought response, and drone footage highlights the drought's impact in England.

news.headline: Record-low Danube River affects tourism and industry as drought and heat grip Central Europe
news.body: As wildfires and successive heatwaves in France and Spain highlight climate change's impact, a severe drought is causing record low water levels on the Danube River, affecting tourism and industry. The river, which flows through 10 countries, has receded to unprecedented lows, exposing rocks and old shipwrecks. In Budapest, the Danube was measured at just 23 centimeters, breaking previous records. River cruise ships are docking upriver, and sightseeing cruises have been canceled. The drought has also affected Hungary and Romania's nuclear power plant operations, exposed a World War II bomb, and ended the summer season for excursion boat operators in Serbia.

As of mid-August 2026, drought impacts continue globally: Lake Mead and Lake Powell both hit record lows, with human remains surfacing at Lake Mead's Boulder Beach. In India, satellite data shows 64% of farmland under drought stress, while Oklahoma endures an extended heat wave with temperatures reaching 106°F. In the UK, England's drought reveals a ghost village beneath Rutland Water reservoir, and hosepipe bans now affect 27 million people. Colorado reports a surge in bear sightings due to diminished wild food sources, and a record-early champagne harvest in France highlights ongoing climate impacts on agriculture.
Severe drought expands in Minnesota, threatening farms, while in Florida, drought is cited as a factor in increased alligator attacks. In Asia, Skymet cuts its 2026 monsoon forecast to 85% of the long-period average, assigning a 70% chance of drought conditions. Meanwhile, new research indicates drought extremes are intensifying more rapidly than in the past, and Colorado launches the Rye Resurgence Project to promote drought-tolerant grain.

logs.summary:
Greece faced severe wildfires in late July and early August 2026, with a major blaze northwest of Athens destroying over 100 homes and burning thousands of hectares. On August 2, two firefighting helicopters collided in mid-air near Psatha, killing two crew members. By August 3, water-dropping aircraft continued to battle the fires, which had been fueled by extreme winds and record-breaking heat, with over 200 fires reported across the country since July 27.
On August 3, the wildfire west of Athens flared up again, requiring continued water-bombing aircraft operations. By August 4, firefighters seized a break in high winds to reinforce containment lines, while some residents returned to damaged homes, though forecasters warned that stronger gusts and rising temperatures were expected to return. The blaze, part of over 200 fires across Greece since late July, remained a threat amid a record-breaking heatwave and drought.

news.headline: Wildfires Rage in Greece as Heat Wave Grips Europe
news.body: In Greece, two firefighters were killed Sunday when two helicopters battling a massive wildfire collided west of Athens. Two other crew members in one of the helicopters were rescued. More than 100 homes were destroyed overnight this weekend in blazes that broke out around the coastal village of Porto Germeno. Hundreds of people have been evacuated. This is a local resident. Giorgos Mavroidis: “It’s not a good situation. This is extremely sad. The wind is very strong and keeps changing direction. It’s difficult to deal with. The firefighters, who are trained and experienced, can’t contain it. How can we?” Meanwhile, Hungary has temporarily shut down the country’s sole nuclear power plant for the first time in more than four decades amid a scorching heat wave and severe drought that triggered water-use restrictions in more than 100 cities and villages. In more related news, Britain’s National Farmers’ Union warns rising heat and a water drought could lead to shortages of certain foods in parts of England. This is at least the third drought in five years, with some areas of England not seeing rain in over a month. Here in the United States, in Washington state, nearly 65,000 people have received evacuation orders amid intensifying wildfires around the city of Spokane. Local officials say blazes in the region have destroyed more than 700 homes and businesses.

A preliminary investigation suggests that a fault in a wind farm's power line may have sparked the devastating Attica-Boeotia wildfire. Rescue crews are working to reunite hundreds of animals displaced by the blaze, while Civil Protection warns of very high fire risk across multiple regions, including Attica, on August 5-6.
On August 6, the Aigosthena fortress near Porto Germeno was reported to have escaped major damage from the four-day wildfire, though some modern site infrastructure was affected.

news.headline: 2 killed when firefighting helicopters collide near Athens as Europe’s wildfire emergency rages
news.body: Greece’s fire department says the collision of two firefighting helicopters battling a major wildfire burning out of control west of Athens left two crew members dead, while another two were recovered alive. The fire department said on Sunday the dead crew members were one Greek and one Danish national, while the two who were recovered alive were one Greek and one British national. Foreign firefighting and helicopter crews are often deployed in Greece to help tackle wildfires during the country’s hot, dry summers. The collision laid bare the danger at the most volatile front of Europe’s wildfire emergency.

news.headline: Europe's hot, dry summer takes its toll with fires in France and Greece, and drought in the UK
news.body: Europe is grappling with a record-breaking hot and dry summer. Water-dropping planes on Monday tackled a major wildfire in Greece while firefighters in France worked to stabilize a blaze in Provence. The United Kingdom recorded its driest July in nearly two centuries. Strong winds returned in Greece, pushing flames into mountain home clusters, destroying farms and property, and closing a highway. In France, firefighters guarded against flare-ups near Bordeaux. The U.K. weather service reported a prolonged heat wave and lack of rainfall. Europe is the fastest-warming continent, with rising temperatures and droughts making wildfires more intense.

logs.summary: In early August 2026, wildfires in western Canada, particularly the Bald Range fire near Summerland, British Columbia, escalated dramatically. The fire burned over 33,000 acres, destroyed approximately 230 homes, and resulted in the death of one woman, prompting evacuation orders for around 20,000 people. In response, British Columbia declared a state of emergency as crews faced challenging conditions from severe drought and windy weather.

logs.summary:
As of August 15, recovery efforts continue with reports of apparent signs of life under rubble in Cali and Pereira, rekindling some hope. Colombia's president asked the US to temporarily suspend tariffs to aid economic recovery, while human-interest stories emerged, including the tragic discovery of a groom-to-be in collapsed hotel rubble and a heartwarming video of a child donating her piggy bank for relief.
A 3-year-old girl was rescued alive from rubble 100 hours after the earthquake struck, offering a rare sign of hope amid the ongoing recovery phase. No other novel developments were reported in this batch.

incidents.summary:
New reports on August 12 indicate that the severe storms in the Midwest have resulted in at least one child killed by a fallen tree in Indiana, a home explosion in Portage, and a software glitch at the National Weather Service that hindered warning dissemination. Power outages have grown to over 700,000 customers, and flooding persists in parts of Indiana and Ohio, with additional storms expected through the afternoon.
ComEd has restored power to more than 80% of the nearly 410,000 Chicagoland customers affected by the severe storms, though Wednesday's storms added over 35,000 new outages and delayed restoration work in the south region. Columbus, Ohio, Mayor Andrew Ginther declared a state of emergency after severe storms damaged multiple neighborhoods, as the governor assessed impacts across the state. Additional severe storms and flooding continue to threaten central Iowa (with tornado warnings expiring but flooding and power outages reported) and the Cincinnati area, where rainfall of 4-6 inches is possible and a flood watch remains in effect.

logs.summary:
A major derecho storm system caused severe flooding across Ohio and Indiana, with Perry County, Ohio recording over 6 inches of rain and Wayne County, Indiana seeing over 9 inches. The National Weather Service confirmed an EF1 tornado touched down in south Columbus on August 11 during the storms. Additional severe thunderstorms and warnings were reported in Phoenix, Siouxland, and Cape Breton, while officials in Ohio warned of overnight flooding risks.
Flash flooding continues in Indiana and Illinois as severe storms batter the Midwest for a sixth straight day, with muddy floodwaters submerging neighborhoods and first responders rescuing people. The National Weather Service in Indianapolis issued a record 14 flash flood warnings in a single day, while deaths and damage from tornadoes and flooding have been reported across the region.

A powerful magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck off the coast of Indonesia's Flores region near Ende on August 14, 2026, toppling buildings and killing at least two people. The shallow quake triggered a tsunami warning for four provinces, prompting mass evacuations before the alert was later lifted. Several strong aftershocks were reported.
The death toll from the magnitude 7.7 earthquake near Ende, Indonesia has risen to at least 38, with dozens injured and many buildings collapsed or damaged. Rescuers are searching for survivors in affected areas, and tsunami waves of less than 1 meter were recorded in several locations before the warning was lifted.

news.headline: Magnitude 7.7 earthquake strikes off Indonesia, tsunami warning issued - West Hawaii Today
news.body: JAKARTA (Reuters) — An earthquake of magnitude 7.7 and several aftershocks struck off the coast of eastern Indonesia early on Saturday, the nation’s geophysics agency BMKG said, while tsunami waves of less than 1 metre (3 feet) were recorded in several areas. Many rushed from their homes, but there were no initial reports of damage from the quake, which was felt strongly for around one minute in regions such as Nagekeo and Bima, said Dodi Yuleova, the spokesperson for the national disaster mitigation agency. A video on Facebook, verified by Reuters as located at a port in Maumere, the main town in Sikka Regency on Flores Island in eastern Indonesia, showed parts of a building collapsing in dust and rubble as people screamed and ran in the street. A hospital in the district of Ende in East Nusa Tenggara Province was moving patients outside, Kompas TV footage showed. BMKG recorded the first quake at 4:58 a.m. (2158 GMT) at a depth of 15 km (9 miles), followed by several aftershocks.

logs.summary:
The death toll from the August 14 M7.7 earthquake off Flores, Indonesia, has risen to at least 47, with rescue teams struggling to reach remote communities due to landslides and damaged infrastructure. Hundreds of personnel have been deployed for search and recovery, while aftershocks and a separate 6.4 quake elsewhere in Indonesia caused additional panic. Authorities warn the toll may increase as communications are restored in cut-off areas.
As of August 16, the death toll from the M7.7 earthquake near Ende, Indonesia, has risen to at least 51–53, with over 5,000 people evacuated and dozens injured. The East Nusa Tenggara governor declared a 14-day emergency, and rescue teams are deploying personnel and aid, including more than Rp4.5 billion in relief supplies, while nearly 1,000 aftershocks have been recorded.

logs.summary:
The death toll from the M7.7 earthquake has risen to at least 68, with over 12,800 displaced and more than 200 injured. A new magnitude 5.9 aftershock struck the Flores region, adding to over 1,600 recorded aftershocks, while rescue teams continue clearing landslides and distributing aid (27-52 tons of supplies) to affected communities. The disaster overshadowed Indonesia's 81st Independence Day celebrations, and President Prabowo Subianto considered visiting the quake-hit areas.
The earthquake's death toll has risen to at least 70, with nearly 1,200 injured and over 2,100 aftershocks recorded. Children are reported to be traumatized and thousands remain displaced, while infrastructure in East Nusa Tenggara is gradually recovering.

news.headline: Fresh 5.9 quake hits Indonesia's Flores region; Death toll from earlier 7.7 tremor rises to 54
news.body: A magnitude 5.9 earthquake struck Indonesia's Flores region early Monday, as the death toll from a powerful 7.7-magnitude earthquake that hit eastern Indonesia days earlier rose to 54, according to the German Research Centre for Geosciences (GFZ) and Indonesia's National Disaster Management Agency (BNPB). The latest earthquake occurred at a depth of around 10 kilometres, with its epicentre initially located at 8.57 degrees south latitude and 121.55 degrees east longitude, as reported by Anadolu News Agency, citing GFZ. The fresh tremor comes days after the magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck six regencies in eastern Flores Island, leaving a trail of destruction across East Nusa Tenggara (NTT) province. According to Xinhua, BNPB chief Suharyanto on Monday said that the death toll from the 7.7-magnitude earthquake had risen to 54, while authorities continued to assess casualties and damage. Rescue teams were providing medical assistance to hundreds of injured people. More than 12,000 people had been left homeless as of Sunday, with homes and public facilities damaged in the quake, Xinhua reported. The Meteorology, Climatology and Geophysics Agency said aftershocks were continuing. Authorities have deployed land, sea and air transportation, including 11 aircraft and helicopters, to deliver relief supplies and support evacuation operations in remote areas, including Palue Island in Sikka regency. A field hospital is also being prepared at Golo Dukal Stadium after the earthquake damaged Manggarai Regional Hospital and disrupted local health services, Xinhua reported. Preliminary BNPB data indicated that 157 homes were severely damaged, while 41 suffered moderate damage and 148 sustained light damage. Critical public infrastructure was also impacted, including 87 educational facilities, 18 healthcare centres, six administrative offices and five places of worship. To support relief operations, BNPB has dispatched extensive emergency supplies to the affected region. In Jakarta, a major airlift operation was launched from Halim Perdanakusuma Air Force Base to transport 50,000 aid packages weighing 275 tonnes. President Prabowo Subianto oversaw the initial dispatch of 10,500 packages that arrived at the airbase for immediate deployment. news.headline: At least 5 dead after powerful 7.7 earthquake hits Indonesia's Flores island
news.body: At least five people were killed after a powerful magnitude 7.7 earthquake hit off the coast of Indonesia's Flores Island on Saturday morning. CNN reported the confirmed death toll, citing updates from Provincial Police Chief Rudi Darmoko to regional media. The main tremor struck around 6 AM local time roughly 68 kilometres northwest of Ende in East Nusa Tenggara province and was followed by a series of aftershocks, CNN reported, citing data from the US Geological Survey (USGS). The USGS estimated that about 500,000 people were exposed to very strong or severe shaking, which damaged buildings and shocked residents awake, forcing them to flee their homes. Indonesia's national disaster mitigation agency, BNPB, noted that an initial tsunami warning was triggered following the quake but was later lifted. The agency added that about 2,000 residents in the Nagekeo regency evacuated as a precautionary measure. Early damage assessments from BNPB indicate that around 15 buildings, including personal homes and government offices, sustained damage, CNN reported. The developments follow a massive earthquake of magnitude 7.4 that jolted Indonesia early on Saturday, according to the National Centre for Seismology (NCS). The earthquake occurred at a depth of 49 km, the NCS said in a post on X."EQ of M
